name: Chicken Achari
description: Tangy Pakistani chicken achari cooked in an onion-tomato and yogurt masala with fennel, nigella, mustard and fenugreek for its characteristic pickling-spice aroma.
ingredients: ½ cup plain yogurt, whisked smooth
Salt and lemon juice to taste
method: Heat the oil and cook the sliced onion until soft and lightly golden.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and chicken and cook, turning the pieces, until the chicken loses its raw exterior colour.
Add the tomatoes, red chilli, turmeric and salt and cook until the tomatoes soften and begin forming a concentrated masala.
Lower the heat and stir in the whisked yogurt gradually so it combines smoothly instead of hitting very high heat all at once.
Lightly crush the fennel, nigella, mustard and fenugreek seeds and add them with the green chillies. Cover and cook gently until the chicken is fully cooked and tender.
Uncover and reduce excess moisture until the masala clings to the chicken, stirring so the spices do not scorch.
Taste first, then add only as much lemon juice as needed to sharpen the tang without overwhelming the achari spices. Serve hot.
image_alt: Pakistani chicken achari with tomato yogurt masala, green chillies and pickling spices
image_caption: Chicken achari finished with fennel, nigella, mustard and fenugreek in a tangy reduced masala.
technique: Achari flavour comes from restraint: lightly crush the pickling spices and add them after the tomato-yogurt base is established. Fenugreek and mustard become harsh if burnt, so do not fry them aggressively at the beginning.
doneness_cues: Tomatoes should cook down until the masala is cohesive before final spice finishing.
Yogurt should be incorporated without visible watery separation.
Chicken should be fully cooked and coated with masala.
Fennel and nigella should smell aromatic, not scorched.
mistakes: Burning mustard or fenugreek seeds in very hot oil.
Adding lots of lemon before tasting the natural tang from yogurt and tomatoes.
Using achari spice in such quantity that it tastes medicinal.
substitutions: Use less fenugreek if your batch is very bitter or strong.
Boneless thigh can be used with a shorter cook.
Lemon is a final adjustment, not a mandatory fixed quantity.
reheating: Reheat gently until hot, adding only a small splash of water if the masala has tightened.
serving: Serve with roti, naan or plain rice and fresh green chilli.
